lines: Monthly GMV trends, order volume, average order value, and cancellation health.

- **Steady GMV, no strong seasonality:** Monthly GMV has held a ₹114–138M band since mid-2023 (partial launch month Jun 2023 aside), peaking at **₹137.9M in Jan 2025** — revenue growth is volume-driven rather than seasonal.

- **Concentrated category mix:** **Electronics drives ~57% of category GMV (₹1.64B)** — more than 3× the next category, Sports & Fitness (₹497M). Combined with a **~12% cancellation rate** (1 in 8 orders), category concentration and cancellations are the two revenue risks to watch.
Revenue concentration, top products, and return behavior by category.

## Key Insights
- **Revenue is highly concentrated:** Electronics drives ~57% of category GMV (₹1.64B) — more than 3× the next category, Sports & Fitness (₹497M). The top 10 products (₹31M–₹42M each, led by Ambrane Power Bank and Godrej Camera Elite) show revenue spread across brands rather than locked in a single hero product.
- **Returns are broad-based, not category-specific:** Return rates sit in a narrow 19.7%–21.5% band across all 10 categories (highest: Toys & Baby 21.5%, Sports & Fitness 21.4%; lowest: Beauty & Health 19.7%). With ~1 in 5 orders returned, the fix needs to be company-wide (packaging, sizing, expectations) rather than targeted at one category.
Customer segmentation, geographic reach, and monthly acquisition trend.

## Key Insights
- **Loyalty skews mid-market, geography skews north/west:** Regular (4,026) and Budget (2,505) customers make up ~65% of the 10K base, with Premium (~1.5K) and New (~1.5K) nearly tied and only ~5% Inactive. Geographically, Uttar Pradesh (1,860) and Maharashtra (1,621) alone hold ~35% of all customers — engagement and revenue risk are concentrated in a handful of states.
- **Acquisition is steady but flat:** New registrations have run ~140–200 per month (avg ~165) every month since mid-2020 with no sustained upward trend. With top-of-funnel volume plateaued, growth must come from converting the large "New" cohort and reactivating the ~480 inactive customers rather than adding signups.
Order fulfillment funnel, payment mix, and return reason analysis.

## Key Insights
- **Fulfillment is healthy but leakage is ~20%:** Of 50K orders, 32.5K (65%) are Delivered and ~7.6K (15%) are still in flight (Processing/Shipped), while 6.0K (12%) were Cancelled and 3.9K (8%) Returned — recovering even a third of that leakage is worth more than new demand.
- **Digital rails dominate payments; return causes are diffuse:** UPI alone carries 35% of orders and all digital methods ~88% (Cash on Delivery just ~12%). Return reasons are strikingly uniform (477–1,196 per reason, no single dominant driver), so cutting returns requires broad fixes — sizing guidance, QC, and delivery accuracy — rather than one targeted change.
Stock status summary, low stock products, and warehouse distribution.

## Key Insights
- **~8% of inventory lines need attention:** 78 of 1,000 stock records are flagged — 76 Low Stock and 2 Out of Stock. Low-stock lines sit far below their reorder points (often 8–50 units on hand against reorder levels of 30–50), so replenishment orders should go out before the next demand cycle.
- **Stock is well balanced across the 6 warehouses:** Available units range from 32.4K (Mumbai-WH1) to 47.4K (Chennai-WH5), a spread of under ~32%. No single warehouse is a bottleneck, but Mumbai-WH1's lower buffer makes it the most exposed to the low-stock lines above.
